verdict.rationale: Amplitude documents an Experiment management API for programmatically creating and controlling flags and experiments, and an official MCP server, so the agent-access half of the story is covered. Nothing in the evidence shows approval workflows or review gates that force programmatic changes through sign-off before they reach production. Copying experiments between projects is not an approval control. Missing for 10: documented approval/review workflows for API/MCP-originated flag changes, any CLI, details of the MCP server's flag tools, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: Use the Experiment management API to programmatically create and control flags and experiments.
Manage flags, experiments, and deployments from CI, scripts, or your own tools with the Experiment APIs.
official MCP server documented at https://amplitude.com/mcp-server
